exposure: Mutations in the SLC19A2 gene (causing Thiamine responsive megaloblastic anemia - TRMA)
cohort: A one-and-a-half-year-old male infant born to non-consanguineous parents.
finding: Early recognition and intervention, particularly cochlear implantation, can significantly improve the quality of life for individuals with Thiamine responsive megaloblastic anemia (TRMA) by reversing symptoms like hearing loss.
